title: J1 — Born abroad
description: A Lao baby gets his first vaccines in Thailand and leaves with signed paper cards.

steps.title: A Lao baby is born in Thailand
steps.headline: Somsack gets his birth vaccines in a Thai hospital — and the only thing that will cross the border with him is a pair of paper cards.

preconditions.title: The issuer's DSC is on the trust list
preconditions.description: **Precondition: the issuer's DSC is on the trust list.** XXR's document signer certificate (DSC), issued under XXR's Country Signing CA (CSCA), was shared with the GDHCN, the Trust Anchor, before any DVC is signed; the GDHCN publishes it as a DID document. Sharing it is not a step of issuing. A DVC signed with a key whose DSC was never shared fails every receiver's trust-list check (STT-VER-006).

steps.narrative:
Khamla gives birth to Somsack on 2025-10-28 at Chiang Rai Provincial
Hospital, away from home. He has no Thai identity number. Dr Anan gives the
Hep B and BCG birth doses and records them with their WHO PreQual product
codes. For each dose, the hospital system does three things:

1. It builds a DVCMinPreQual payload: STT-PAY-001…005 and STT-PAY-007, with subclaim −6 (STT-SEL-003). No identity document is needed (STT-PAY-005).
2. It prepares the CWT and the bytes to sign: STT-CWT-001…005, STT-ISS-004.
3. It has XXR's key sign them (STT-COS-002, STT-COS-006), then finishes the HC1 text: STT-COS-001, STT-ZIP-001, STT-B45-001, STT-HC1-001, STT-QR-001.

Khamla leaves with two paper DVCs.
*In the demo:* the library tests use the WHO guide's own two signed HC1
strings ([QR Code Generation §12](https://smart.who.int/trust/qr_code_generation.html)),
which verify against the live DEV trust list under the same XXR key. Somsack's
DVC payloads are illustrative, as in VaxLink. Live issuance in the app uses a
TEST-ONLY key (STT-ISS-003), whose DSC is not on the GDHCN list, so its DVCs
do not verify in J3.

experiences.doing: Gives Hep B and BCG birth doses and prints two signed QR vaccine cards.
experiences.feeling: “He isn’t Thai, but he still needs a record he can take home.”

experiences.doing: Is born, and gets his Hep B and BCG birth doses within hours.
experiences.feeling: “Two small jabs, and a record that will follow him.”

experiences.doing: Gives birth away from home and receives two paper cards at discharge.
experiences.feeling: “Will anyone back home believe these papers?”

steps.painPoint: The baby has no Thai ID number, so his records would normally stay locked inside the Thai hospital’s system.
steps.enabler: A digitally signed QR card travels with the family — no ID number or database lookup needed.
steps.policy: Babies born abroad can get a verifiable vaccine record before they have the host country’s civil registration or a national ID — and registering the birth at home still matters.

handoff.summary: Two paper cards go home with Khamla
handoff.payload: Signed DVC: HC1: prefix → CBOR + COSE_Sign1

whatIf.scenario: The cards are lost on the way home.
whatIf.outcome: The doses still happened, but no proof travels. Lao clinicians must re-vaccinate or rely on memory.

steps.technicalSummary: Thailand signs the record once. From then on, anyone on the WHO trust network can check it, with no database lookup and no national ID.

Vaccines coded with WHO PreQual product codes
